summary: Created Fleet Internal CA on node1, issued a constrained node2 TLS certificate, installed the CA into both RHEL system trust stores, and configured persistent nginx HTTPS on node2:8443. Both nodes retained the existing RHEL 10.0 release and 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 kernel. One-at-a-time restart testing proved persistence and recovery.
actions_performed: Installed vendor-supported RHEL OpenSSL packages and nginx.
Created a 3072-bit Fleet Internal CA; its private key remains root-only on node1.
Generated node2's private key locally and issued a CA-signed server certificate containing DNS:node2 and IP:10.100.65.11 SANs.
Installed Fleet Internal CA as a system trust anchor on both nodes.
Configured nginx for TLS 1.2/1.3 on port 8443, enabled it at boot, and opened only TCP 8443 for the new service.
Verified trusted HTTPS by hostname and IP, certificate/key matching, hostname rejection, TLS 1.3, and absence of the CA private key on node2.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create Fleet Internal CA on node1
evidence.summary: Shows CN=Fleet Internal CA, CA:TRUE, certificate-signing usage, protected key permissions, and stable SHA-256 fingerprint.

evidence.requirement: Issue a TLS certificate for node2
evidence.summary: Proves the CSR SANs, CA signature, certificate/key match, CA:FALSE, serverAuth, DNS/IP identities, and live presentation.

evidence.requirement: Install the CA as a trusted system authority on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Both system trust stores identify Fleet Internal CA as an authority trust anchor before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Serve HTTPS on node2 port 8443 persistently and securely
evidence.summary: nginx is enabled and active, firewalld permits 8443, only the requested HTTPS listener is present, remote trust validation succeeds over TLS 1.3, and incorrect hostnames are rejected.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.
Captures healthy baseline, acknowledged safe reboot, boot ID change from f5c00b57… to bf05086a…, and recovered CA files, trust, certificate validation, and remote HTTPS access.
Captures healthy baseline, acknowledged safe reboot, boot ID change from 7217fc31… to 519d39cd…, and recovered nginx, firewall, trust, certificate/key, content, and HTTPS listener.
